q: Which metals may NOT be used for urinal tailpieces or traps?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Urine attacks brass and copper.

q: How is a drainage system air-tested?
o: By smoke only, with no gauge
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Drainage tests: water test with at least 3 m of head held for 15 minutes, or air test at 34.5 kPa (254 mm of mercury) held for 15 minutes.

q: What surface must a public shower floor have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Shower rules: floor sloped 2–4% to the drain, non-skid surface, compartment at least 1.78 m high, threshold 51 to 228 mm deep and 25.4 mm lower than the floor outside.

q: Which wash trays are prohibited in buildings for human habitation?
o: Fixed trays of wood, concrete or tile
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Site-built trays are porous and cannot be kept sanitary.

q: What happens to the plumbing of a building moved to a new site?
o: The plumbing work is tested again
Nothing, if it was tested before
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Moving a building can crack joints, so the system must pass a new test.

q: How are copper shower pan joints made?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Metal pans must be watertight at every seam.

q: What must screws and bolts that fasten fixtures be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Fasteners near water rust away unless they are brass, stainless or similar.

q: What must be done with existing plumbing in a building?
o: Left as it is, even if it is leaking
Maintained by the city, not the owner
Kept in repair so it causes no nuisance
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: The code applies to maintenance too, not just new work.

q: What happens when plumbing fails a test?
o: The defects are corrected and it is tested again
It is approved with a note
The permit is cancelled for good
The owner pays a fine and it is approved
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Work is approved only when it passes.

q: Under the plumbing code, is a floor drain a plumbing fixture?
o: Only if it has a trap primer
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: A floor drain receives waste water and discharges it to the drainage system, so it is a fixture.

q: Where does a fixture's overflow pipe connect?
o: To the outlet side of the trap
To the inlet side of the fixture trap
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Connecting before the trap keeps sewer gas out of the overflow.

q: When may new plumbing be covered up?
o: Before testing, if the owner agrees
Only after the building is occupied
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: The inspector must see the work before it is hidden.

q: How deep must a shower threshold be above the drain?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Shower rules: floor sloped 2–4% to the drain, non-skid surface, compartment at least 1.78 m high, threshold 51 to 228 mm deep and 25.4 mm lower than the floor outside.

q: What is the minimum tailpiece size for lavatories and drinking fountains?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Sinks, dishwashers, laundry trays and tubs need 38 mm tailpieces.

q: How is a drainage system water-tested?
o: With 0.5 m of head for 1 minute
With 30 m of head for 24 hours
With 3 m of head for 15 minutes
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Drainage tests: water test with at least 3 m of head held for 15 minutes, or air test at 34.5 kPa (254 mm of mercury) held for 15 minutes.

q: What is the minimum height of a shower compartment?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Shower rules: floor sloped 2–4% to the drain, non-skid surface, compartment at least 1.78 m high, threshold 51 to 228 mm deep and 25.4 mm lower than the floor outside.

q: Where may drinking fountains NOT be installed?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: A fountain in a toilet room could be contaminated.

q: What air pressure may be used instead of a water test on water supply piping?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Water supply piping works under pressure, so it is tested far higher than drainage.

q: How are lead shower pan joints made?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Lead is fused to lead with a torch.

q: What must the joint between a fixture and the wall or floor be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: A leaky joint soaks the wall and breeds bacteria.

q: Who must keep plumbing in a safe and sanitary condition?
o: The owner or person in charge of the building
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Once a building is in use, maintenance falls to its owner.

q: Who provides the equipment, materials and labor for plumbing tests?
o: The owner of the next lot
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: The inspector only witnesses.

q: How many urinals may one manual flushometer valve serve?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: An automatic flush tank may flush several urinals, but a manual flushometer serves only one.

q: Which of these is allowed for special-use fixtures such as laboratory sinks?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Other listed materials include lead-lined, copper-base or nickel-copper alloy, and corrosion-resistant steel.

q: What is issued when plumbing work is complete and passes its final test?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: The certificate lets the system be used.

q: How does a shower threshold relate to the floor outside?
o: It is level with the floor outside
It is 25.4 mm lower than the floor outside
It is 150 mm higher than the floor outside
It is 300 mm lower than the floor outside
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Shower rules: floor sloped 2–4% to the drain, non-skid surface, compartment at least 1.78 m high, threshold 51 to 228 mm deep and 25.4 mm lower than the floor outside.

q: What is the minimum tailpiece size for sinks, dishwashers, laundry trays and bathtubs?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Lavatories and drinking fountains may use 32 mm.

q: How is a section of drainage set up for a water test?
o: Only the lowest opening plugged, with no filling
All openings plugged and the pipe left empty
All openings plugged except the highest, which is filled
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Drainage tests: water test with at least 3 m of head held for 15 minutes, or air test at 34.5 kPa (254 mm of mercury) held for 15 minutes.

q: What must be provided at the base of every soil and waste stack?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Stack bases are where blockages form, so they need a way in.

q: Which water closets are prohibited?
o: Those with hidden seals or unwashed walls
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Hidden spaces trap waste and cannot be cleaned.

q: What must a building sewer be when tested?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: A sewer that leaks contaminates the soil and lets roots in.

q: In a gang shower, how far apart at most may gutter drains be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Close drains keep water from pooling along the gutter.

q: How must the water supply to special fixtures be protected?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Lab and medical fixtures could draw dangerous fluids into the supply.

q: How is a shower receptor (pan) tested?
o: Filled to the threshold and checked
By pouring one bucket of water in
By a smoke test through the drain
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: The pan must hold water for the test period.

q: How much notice must be given before a plumbing inspection?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: The Plumbing Official needs time to schedule the visit.

q: How many urinals may an automatic flush tank serve?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: A manual flushometer valve serves only one urinal.

q: What type of water closet bowl is used in public toilets?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: The longer bowl is easier to keep clean.

q: Who must be present when plumbing is tested?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: The inspector must witness the test for it to count.

q: Which of these may a shower receptor be made of?
o: Vitreous china, tile or enameled metal
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Receptors must be smooth, waterproof and easy to clean.

q: How large must the open area of a fixture strainer be?
o: A quarter of the outlet area
At least equal to the outlet area
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: A strainer with less open area than the pipe would slow drainage.

q: May covered plumbing be ordered uncovered?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Work covered before approval can be ordered opened.

q: What slope must a shower floor have toward the drain?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 4–5
n: Shower rules: floor sloped 2–4% to the drain, non-skid surface, compartment at least 1.78 m high, threshold 51 to 228 mm deep and 25.4 mm lower than the floor outside.
